text.p: These are leading stories in this morning's Paris newspapers.
LES ECHOS
- French people vote for change. Suspense is total ahead of second round vote. Abstention rate near to 31 percent, comparable to 1993 presidential election.

- Europe makes progress on institutional reforms. A special European Union summit in Noordwijk in the Netherlands on Friday paved the way for success in a summit in Amsterdam next month on institutional reform. French President Jacques Chirac supports German proposal to limit European Commission to 20 members.
- France Telecom aims to increase share of income made abroad. "The result of the election in France will not change our policies on international development," France Telecom head Michel Bon said.
- Time Warner U.S.-based media group considers buying a 35 percent stake in CGV and a 10 percent stake in CanalSatellite.
- Groupe Paribas redefines its presence in Belgium.
LA TRIBUNE
- Left-wing forces in a position to win the second run of the parliamentary election. The RPR and UDF coalition score historic low. Far-right party National Front confirms its position.
- France Telecom aims for international presence but its ambitions do not always match those of its ally Deutsche Telekom
- Axa cuts to under 10 percent its stake in the BNP .
L'AGEFI
-- Financial markets face a possible sharing of power between left and right forces.
-- Paribas sells Belgian subsidiary to Bacob-Arco group.
-- SGS-Thomson Electroelectronics semi-conductors expected to take advantage of a pickup in the sector expected for 1997.
LE FIGARO
-- Ruling coalition in difficulty ahead of the second round of the parliamentary election.
LIBERATION
- Air France expects 1996/97 accounts to provide a "an excellent surprise." which would be the first return to profit since 1989.
